# Hash-pinned install set for ci.yml's "Install verification test deps" step.
#
# Direct requirements: pytest pyyaml requests flask
#
# The lint job ("Syntax & Lint") runs on ubuntu-latest / CPython 3.9 and then
# runs ~54 guard test files through pytest. It was installing those four with
# a bare `pip install`, so the guards that decide whether this repo's code is
# sound ran against whatever the index served that minute.
#
# Why this file and not ci-tests.txt: that set is resolved for CPython 3.11
# and pins pytest==9.1.1, requests==2.34.2 and click==8.5.0, none of which
# install on 3.9. This job runs on 3.9 DELIBERATELY -- it is the floor
# setup.py advertises, and running the guards there means they are exercised
# on the interpreter 0.12.753 broke on. So the two sets cannot be merged
# until that floor moves.
#
# These versions are what `pip install pytest pyyaml requests flask` already
# resolves to on 3.9 today (pytest 9.x and requests 2.33+ both declare
# Requires-Python >= 3.10), so pinning changes the artifacts' provenance,
# not the versions the job has been running.
#
# NOTE FOR A DEPENDABOT BUMP HERE: a proposed move to a release that dropped
# 3.9 cannot install on this job at all, and `--require-hashes` fails the
# whole step rather than the one package. That failure lands on the bump PR,
# where the lint job runs on every PR -- it is the signal, not a flake. Lift
# the 3.9 floor first, or leave the pin.
#
# WHAT STAYING ON THESE VERSIONS ACCEPTS. Four names here sit at the LAST
# release that installs on 3.9, and each is named by published advisories
# whose only fixes require 3.10+. Measured 2026-10-02 against PyPI
# Requires-Python and OSV:
#
#   click==8.5.0     ceiling; 8.2.0+ needs >=3.10.
#                    GHSA-47fr-3ffg-hgmw (fixed 8.3.3)
#   pytest==9.1.1    ceiling; 9.0.0+ needs >=3.10.
#                    GHSA-6w46-j5rx-g56g (fixed 9.0.3)
#   requests==2.34.2 ceiling; 2.33.0+ needs >=3.10.
#                    GHSA-gc5v-m9x4-r6x2 (fixed 2.33.0)
#   urllib3==2.8.0   ceiling; 2.7.0+ needs >=3.10.
#                    GHSA-qccp-gfcp-xxvc, GHSA-mf9v-mfxr-j63j (fixed 2.7.0),
#                    GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g,
#                    GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw (fixed 2.8.0)
#
# So these are CAPPED, not stale. The sweep that raised ten other CI pin sets
# to urllib3 2.8.0 (#6213) could not raise this one, and an audit that reports
# any of the above as "fix available" has read the fix version without reading
# its Requires-Python. Re-deriving that costs a tick every time; this block is
# here so the next reader does not have to.
#
# The acceptance is deliberate, and the exposure it carries is narrow. The only
# job that installs this file is ci.yml's "Syntax & Lint", which runs this
# repo's static guard tests -- workflow-YAML validity, pin guards, drift
# checks. `requests` and `flask` are here so pytest can COLLECT at all
# (tests/conftest.py imports requests at module scope), and the one requests
# call site in that conftest is a health probe against a local dashboard. None
# of the urllib3/requests advisories above -- which concern HTTPS proxy TLS
# handling, sensitive headers on cross-origin redirects, and decompressing or
# buffering remote response bodies -- has a reachable trigger in a job that
# fetches nothing. `click` arrives transitively via flask and nothing here
# calls click.edit(), the function its advisory is in. The pytest advisory is
# tmpdir handling where another local user can race it; the runner is
# single-tenant and ephemeral. All of it is CI-only -- no released wheel, no
# user machine.
#
# Why not the environment-marker trick ci-api-tests.txt uses: that file serves
# a matrix spanning BOTH interpreters, so carrying each name twice behind
# mutually exclusive python_full_version markers gets its 3.11 cells the fixed
# releases while its 3.9 cell keeps the installable ones. This file has no
# 3.10+ consumer -- "Syntax & Lint" is a single 3.9 job -- so a marker split
# here would add a second copy of every pin that nothing would ever resolve.
#
# The acceptance ends when this job's interpreter moves off 3.9: at that point
# this file folds into ci-tests.txt, which already pins the fixed releases of
# all four.
#
# Installed with `pip install --require-hashes`, which refuses to install
# anything not listed here with a matching hash. Each version lists the
# sha256 of EVERY distribution PyPI publishes for it (every platform wheel,
# plus the sdist), so the pin does not quietly depend on the runner resolving
# to the same artifact this file was generated against.
#
# Regenerate with:
#   uv pip compile --generate-hashes --python-version 3.9 --no-header \
#     -o .github/requirements/ci-lint-verify.txt -  # pytest pyyaml requests flask
blinker==1.9.0 \
    --hash=sha256:b4ce2265a7abece45e7cc896e98dbebe6cead56bcf805a3d23136d145f5445bf \
    --hash=sha256:ba0efaa9080b619ff2f3459d1d500c57bddea4a6b424b60a91141db6fd2f08bc
